subject: Regional connectivity lag — customer steps, temporary routing, and evidence request
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <ops@acme-retail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2029-07-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Regional connectivity lag — immediate guidance and temporary routing options

Jordan — quick summary and immediate next steps from Redwood. We observed an upstream network flap at one of our cloud provider POPs that originated ~08:00 PDT and affected connectivity into US-EAST-1, EU-WEST-3, and APAC-SG for ~40 minutes. Impact: increased tail latency for streaming responses and intermittent 5xx errors for a subset of tenants that had sticky regional affinity.

What we did (short):
- Smart routing engaged: traffic attempted transparent failover to cross-region pools; this reduced complete outages but increased median latency for some sessions.
- KV cache priming was invalidated for a fraction of sessions after the region switch which caused token/regeneration spikes.
- We enabled an emergency regional bypass for affected tenant IDs and applied a temporary HTTP-only endpoint to preserve session continuity.

What we recommend for Acme (immediate):
1) Switch to the regional-read endpoint we can provision for you (details below) — this pins requests to our dedicated US-West nodes while we monitor upstream repairs.
2) Apply client-side retry with exponential backoff (start at 150ms, cap 1600ms) and increase connection keepalive to avoid re-negotiation.
3) Short-term DNS TTL adjustment: set your SDK host TTL to 30s while we stabilize routing.
4) If you have request-level routing logic, enable 'prefer-local' flag to prefer your APAC region for latency-sensitive calls once we return APAC capacity.

Attachments: redwood-temporary-routing-playbook.pdf (playbook excerpt), acme-audit-evidence-template.docx (we'll need a few logs for your internal audit).

I'll provision the temporary endpoint now and follow up with config snippets. If you want us to make the SDK swap for you, say the word and we can queue it as an emergency change with tracking.

—David
David Kim
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Mills <ops@acme-retail.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2029-07-15T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional connectivity lag — immediate guidance and temporary routing options

Thanks, David. Appreciate the fast summary. Quick clarifying Qs:
- Do you expect token billing to spike while KV cache warms? If so, we need a heads-up for our finance ops.
- Please send the exact temporary endpoint and any header we need to set.

Also attaching the minimal info you asked for: our tenant IDs  and a short list of impacted services. We'll send fuller logs shortly.

Jordan
Ops Lead, Acme Retail

> Jordan — quick summary and immediate next steps from Redwood. We observed an upstream network flap...

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2029-07-15T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional connectivity lag — immediate guidance and temporary routing options

Jordan — answers and the config snippet below. Short answer: yes, you may see a transient increase in token usage while cache warms, but we've estimated the increase to be under ~8% over the next 30 minutes for your typical workload mix. We'll annotate billing so you can reconcile.

Temporary endpoint (HTTP only):
https://us-west-temp.api.redwood.ai/acme-tenant-001
Add header: X-Redwood-Bypass: regional-emergency

SDK swap (one-line curl example):
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"endpoint":"https://us-west-temp.api.redwood.ai/acme-tenant-001","headers":{"X-Redwood-Bypass":"regional-emergency"}}' 
  https://config.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/acme-tenant-001/override

I'll provision the endpoint and leave it in place until we confirm upstream stabilization plus one hour of healthy telemetry. If you'd rather have Redwood handle the SDK change, confirm and we will do an emergency config change and schedule a post-change rollback window.

Also uploading the playbook excerpt to the linked Drive for your SREs.

—David

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2029-07-15T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Regional connectivity lag — immediate guidance and temporary routing options

FYI — ops control plane reports upstream fiber maintenance in APAC was extended; cloud provider expects full restoration by 13:30 PDT. EU and US had short-lived BGP convergence issues we mitigated with route announces.

Action items (internal):
- I provisioned two extra warming hosts in US-WEST and flagged their pools for Acme.
- I set temporary caching policy to aggressive pre-warm for tenant acme-tenant-001 and queued a cache rehydrate job.
- Preparing audit bundle (requesting the customer confirm the exact time ranges for logs).

I'll post a status update to the incident page in 30 minutes.

—Marcus
Platform Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Regional connectivity lag — immediate guidance and temporary routing options (final update)

Elena — short note for finance: 
"During an upstream cloud provider network convergence event on 2029-07-15 between 07:58–08:40 PDT, we executed a temporary cross-region routing and cache rehydrate to preserve service availability. This may cause a short-term increase in token volume while caches warm and sessions re-establish; Redwood will annotate usage for Acme Retail for reconciliation and will not bill unexplained duplicate token charges. Estimated transient increase: ~<8% over a 30–60 minute window."

Yes — the user-facing slowdown you saw from 07:58–08:26 PDT lines up with our telemetry and the initial convergence.

Next steps:
- We will keep the temporary endpoint available until 16:15 PDT.
- Incident postmortem (root cause + timelines + remediation) will be published by EOD tomorrow and the audit bundle delivered by Wednesday.
- Please upload the log windows you have and fill the attached evidence template; we'll merge and return a consolidated bundle.

Thanks for the fast coordination. If you want us to run the SDK swap, confirm by 16:00 and we'll execute with a tracked change.

—David
